one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 1.7x fair value. Interesting below about $212.

profile.what: Microsoft sells Azure cloud computing, Microsoft 365 (Office, Teams, Outlook), Windows, LinkedIn, GitHub, Dynamics business software and Xbox gaming. It is a large investor in OpenAI and is building AI into all its products through Copilot.
profile.money: Mostly subscriptions and usage fees from companies. Azure is the fastest-growing part, charging by computing used. Microsoft 365 charges per user per month. Windows earns licence fees from PC makers. It is spending well over $100 billion a year on data centres for AI.
profile.valued: Microsoft is valued on P/E and free cash flow at a premium for its durable growth. The debate is whether AI spending earns an adequate return: its multiple moves with Azure growth and with the size of its capital spending.

summary.sentence: A dominant enterprise software and cloud business betting very large sums on AI capacity.
strengths: Azure and AI services are growing quickly on an already huge base.
Operating margin above 45% at this scale is exceptional.
Revenue up roughly two-thirds in four years.
risks: Free cash flow has fallen while earnings rose, because of AI data-centre capex.
P/FCF near 68 means the price leans on future cash, not today's.
AI returns are unproven at this level of spending.

meaning.what_it_does: Sells the software and cloud infrastructure most businesses run on: Azure, Microsoft 365, Windows, LinkedIn, GitHub and gaming.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Recurring subscriptions (Microsoft 365, Dynamics), usage-based cloud computing (Azure) and licences.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Enterprises are deeply embedded in its tools; AI copilots and Azure AI services give existing customers new reasons to spend more.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: If AI spending fails to earn a return, the record capex becomes a drag on free cash flow for years; or a cloud price war erodes margins.

moat.summary: Replacing Office, Teams, Active Directory and Azure across a large company is costly and risky, so customers rarely leave. Only Amazon and Google can match its cloud scale.

industry.summary: Enterprise software is sticky, but the AI infrastructure race is moving fast and demands enormous capital.

management.summary: Has rebuilt the company around cloud and AI with excellent execution; equity has nearly tripled in five years. The open question is the return on today's record capex.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow, capex held at depreciation: $92.0B a year: operating cash flow less depreciation and stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). Capex is running at 3.5x depreciation, so most of it is expansion, not upkeep. (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 9–15% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 47%; cost of capital 9.4%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
